tutorial.info: Gleek is a three-player game on a 44-card pack (a standard deck minus the 2s and 3s) and **every one of its four stages moves points inside a single deal**. (1) The stock is auctioned: the eldest hand must open at 12 and may not pass, raises go up in twos, and the buyer pays half the bid to each opponent before taking the seven stock cards other than the turn-up and throwing seven of their own. (2) The ruff: the best single-suit total (A=11, courts=10, numerals at face value) collects 2 from each opponent, and a mournival of aces beats any ruff whatsoever. (3) The melds: three or four of a rank above ten, paid by each opponent — aces 4/8, kings 3/6, queens 2/4, jacks 1/2. (4) Twelve tricks, worth 3 apiece plus trump honours. The par each seat settles against is **the points this deal actually held** divided by three — the turn-up and the buyer's discards never reach the table, so that can be less than the 81 a deal could hold.
